stories.title: Egypt fines prominent editor Lina Attalah and shuts independent news outlet Mada Masr
bullet_points: Warnings of escalating clampdown on press freedom come after Cairo court convicts Attalah of managing an unlicensed website  Lina Attalah, a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, has been released from detention by Egypt’s authorities and had her website ordered to be shut down by a court amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in the country.
Attalah was taken briefly into custody after a Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, prompting fresh international concerns over press freedom in Egypt.

stories.title: Africa’s ‘unprecedented’ Ebola outbreak could reach UK, says top health official
bullet_points: Jean Kaseya, of the Africa CDC, warns of the illness spreading like Covid unless more funding is secured to increase preparedness and possible treatment  The “unprecedented”  spread of the Ebola outbreak  means it could reach the UK and other countries, according to one of Africa’s top health officials.

As the current outbreak reached  10,000 cases, with almost 5,000 deaths , Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), compared the outbreak to the Covid pandemic, which first took hold in China before spreading to countries across the world, claiming millions of lives, and ravaging health systems and economies.

stories.title: Brazil’s victory for the planet and democracy: seven lessons from Lula’s win
bullet_points: The trouncing of the far right provides a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France    Thank you, Brazil, for demonstrating how the far right can be trounced while protection for the Amazon is strengthened.
This should provide much needed inspiration and, more practically, a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France.

The astonishing comeback victory of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Sunday’s presidential runoff against his extreme right challenger Flavío Bolsonaro has brought oceans of rapturous supporters on to the streets, while also thrilling conservationists, climate activists and social justice campaigners across the world.
